faqs.a: Title Case capitalises the first letter of every word: 'hello world' becomes 'Hello World'. Sentence case capitalises only the first letter of each sentence: 'hello world. how are you' becomes 'Hello world. How are you'.
faqs.q: What is the difference between Title Case and Sentence case?

faqs.a: Yes. If your text was typed with Caps Lock stuck on ('hELLO'), the Inverse option flips every letter's case and gives you 'Hello'. Then pick the case you actually want.
faqs.q: I typed everything with Caps Lock on. Can this fix it?

faqs.a: The tool uses standard Unicode case rules, so accented Latin letters like e to E convert correctly. Scripts without case (Arabic, Hindi, Chinese) are left untouched, which is the correct behaviour.
faqs.q: Does it work with accented or non-English letters?

faqs.a: Alternating case flips every letter: 'hello' becomes 'HeLlO'. It is mostly a joke or stylistic format for social media. The tool skips non-letters when counting the alternation, so punctuation does not break the pattern.
No. The tool changes letter case only. It does not fix spelling, grammar, or punctuation, and Title Case will capitalise small words (like 'and' or 'the') that some style guides keep lowercase.
faqs.q: Will Title Case follow APA or Chicago style rules?

faqs.a: Yes. It runs entirely in your browser. Nothing you paste is uploaded, stored, or seen by anyone else.

case-converter.formula:
upper: every letter -> UPPERCASE
lower: every letter -> lowercase
title: first letter of each word Upper, the rest lower
  'hello world' -> 'Hello World'
sentence: whole text lowercased, then the first letter after each '.', '!', '?' (or the start) -> Upper
  'hello. world' -> 'Hello. World'
alternating: letters flip Upper/lower/Upper..., skipping non-letters
  'hello' -> 'HeLlO'
inverse: each letter's case is swapped
  'hELLO' -> 'Hello'

keyFacts: UPPERCASE makes every letter capital: useful for headings and emphasis.
lowercase makes every letter small: useful for URLs and code.
Title Case capitalises the first letter of each word: 'hello world' becomes 'Hello World'.
Sentence case capitalises only the first letter of each sentence.
aLtErNaTiNg cAsE flips every letter for a playful, stylised look.
InVeRsE case swaps each letter's case: handy when Caps Lock was stuck on.

limitations: Changes letter case only - it does not fix spelling or grammar.

Sentence case splits on '.', '!' and '?' only; abbreviations like 'e.g.' may confuse it.
Scripts without letter case (Arabic, Hindi, Chinese) are unaffected, which is correct but means nothing changes for them.
